title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 77 (Duty to register charges)

content.overview: Section 77 requires registration of charges created by a company, within the prescribed period, with the Registrar, failing which the charge is void against a liquidator or creditor.
content.glance: Section 77 requires registration of charges created by a company, within the prescribed period, with the Registrar, failing which the charge is void against a liquidator or creditor.
content.study: A company creating a charge on its property or undertaking, in or outside India, must register particulars with the Registrar within thirty days, extendable as the section and rules allow on application and additional fees. Registration gives constructive notice under s. 80. A charge not registered in time is void against the liquidator and any creditor, but the money secured becomes immediately payable. The company remains liable to register; a charge holder may apply under s. 78. Satisfaction is reported under s. 82. The duty covers modification of charge as s. 79 applies the same regime.

Registration gives constructive notice under s. 80. A charge not registered in time is void against the liquidator and any creditor, but the money secured becomes immediately payable. The company remains liable to register; a charge holder may apply under s. 78. Satisfaction is reported under s. 82. The duty covers modification of charge as s. 79 applies the same regime.

examples.title: Late charge
examples.body: A charge filed after the permitted window does not prevail against the liquidator.

examples.title: Immediate payable
examples.body: The debt itself is not extinguished; it becomes immediately payable.

hypotheticals.facts: A charge filed after the permitted window does not prevail against the liquidator.
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 77 requires registration of charges created by a company, within the prescribed period, with the Registrar, failing which the charge is void against a liquidator or creditor.

distinctions: Registration under s. 77 perfects the charge against liquidator and creditors. It is not the same as stamping, or as CERSAI registration of security interest under the SARFAESI framework.

misconceptions.correction: Section 77 requires registration of charges created by a company, within the prescribed period, with the Registrar, failing which the charge is void against a liquidator or creditor.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Does non-registration wipe out the debt?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. The charge is vulnerable against the liquidator and creditors; the secured sum becomes immediately payable.
